title: Post from @PrairieDad_Larkin — "Dead Birds at Prairie Wind"

fields.avatarBrief: man in his thirties in a blaze-orange stocking cap and a canvas chore coat, selfie in a pickup cab with a toddler car seat visible behind him
fields.text: Drove past the Prairie Wind turkey barns this morning and there was a dump trailer FULL of dead birds out back. It's spreading!! #BirdFlu #CalderCounty
fields.attachedImageBrief: slightly blurry phone photo taken through a pickup's side window from a gravel county road, frosty ditch in the foreground; long white turkey barns about 200 yards away, with a small tarp-covered dump trailer parked behind the end barn; a few white feathers caught on the tarp edge; cold, clear early-morning light, no people visible

comments.author: Kayla R.
comments.text: Omg that's like 5 miles from us. Do we need to put our ducks down?? Somebody from the county please answer!!

comments.author: Dale V.
comments.text: Every turkey farm has a dead trailer out back every day of the year, it gets hauled to rendering. Doesn't mean anything. And quit driving up farm lanes, you're the ones who'll carry something in.

comments.author: Shelly N.
comments.text: First Larkin Ridge now Prairie Wind. Why is nobody telling us anything??

instructorNote: Red herring. Hand the post to the PIO, then read or hand over the two follow-ups: at 09:21 the Northland 9 News assignment desk emails pio@caldercountymn.example, "We're hearing a SECOND outbreak at the Prairie Wind complex. Can you confirm for our noon cut-in?", and at 09:24 complex manager Lena Halvorsen texts the industry liaison seat, "That's our normal daily dead-haul trailer. 11 hens yesterday out of 45,000, about normal. Water use flat. No vet call, no samples submitted. Please tell people to stop driving up to my barns." Watch for three things. PROD should pass the manager's report to the Board, which owns any designation. The PIO should call the Board's PIO and then tell Northland 9 there is one presumptive premises and no report of illness or testing at any other premises. The PIO should not name Prairie Wind, call it "disease-free" or give zone sizes (CCACMP 10), and should ask the public to stay off farm property.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Slightly blurry candid phone photo taken through the passenger-side window of a pickup truck stopped on a gravel county road, edge of the window frame and a faint reflection visible on the glass. A frosty roadside ditch with pale frozen grass fills the foreground. About 200 yards away across a flat harvested field, a row of long low white turkey barns with metal roofs and plain sidewalls. Behind the end barn sits a small dump trailer covered with a dark tarp, a few white feathers caught on the tarp edge. Cold, clear early-morning light with long shadows, pale blue sky, empty rural landscape, uneasy mood.
